With zero authoritative durations, the timing data that would let us optimize execution is exactly what the detector dropped — there is no slow-experiment list to act on from the authoritative block.
improvements_suggested: Fix the milestone-scoped timing detector's commit-attribution scan so it attributes experiment commits to the active milestone. This false-zero has now recurred for ~12 consecutive milestones and is the single highest-value operational-tooling fix; without it every retro is data-blind.
Until the detector is fixed, give the retro a changelog-window fallback timing source for the active milestone so per-experiment narrative is grounded on-disk rather than reported as empty.
Gate the operational-retro on a non-empty authoritative timing block OR a changelog fallback, so a detector false-zero does not silently produce a data-free retro that reads as 'nothing ran'.

When the resumable Sudoku-Extreme training continues into .383 (per the changelog the baseline is still climbing toward 0.87), keep both 3090s engaged — the snapshot shows the full 48GB free, so a single training run is leaving one GPU idle.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Root-cause and fix the milestone-scoped timing detector false-zero (commit-attribution scan) — it has dropped per-experiment timing for ~12 consecutive milestones and is why this retro has no execution data to optimize.

Add a changelog-window fallback timing source to the operational-retro path so the narrative is grounded on-disk when the detector returns zero, and gate the retro so an empty timing block cannot pass silently.

Parallelize the continuing resumable Sudoku-Extreme training across both idle 3090s (48GB free per the snapshot) to cut the per-pass wall time that is now the .382/.383 baseline-convergence bottleneck.
meta_reflection: The honest operational signal this milestone is not a speed number but a detector defect: an authoritative timing block that false-zeros while the milestone demonstrably ran (exp4126-exp4133 per the on-disk changelog) makes the operational retro data-blind. Fixing the commit-attribution scan is worth more than any single experiment's speedup because it restores the per-experiment timing the retro exists to analyze; the estimated_time_savings_pct is a conservative estimate predicated on that fix surfacing the real bottlenecks plus dual-GPU use on the continuing training.
